name: Fibromuscular Dysplasia of Renal Arteries

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No universally accepted formal criteria; diagnosis based on imaging and clinical presentation

criteria.description: Characteristic 'string of beads' appearance or focal stenosis on angiography or CT/MR angiography
Presence of secondary hypertension, often resistant or early onset
Exclusion of atherosclerotic renal artery disease and other causes of renal artery stenosis
Symptoms consistent with renal ischemia such as flank pain or abdominal bruit

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Imaging evidence of characteristic arterial changes plus clinical evidence of secondary hypertension with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis primarily relies on imaging modalities combined with clinical presentation; biopsy rarely performed.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Renal artery stenosis with 'string of beads' angiographic appearance
searchTerms: narrowed kidney artery with beaded look
renal artery narrowing with string of beads
kidney artery stenosis with beaded appearance

pathognomonic.notes: Often resistant or early onset hypertension

common.notes: Audible vascular bruit over affected renal artery
May be related to hypertension or ischemia

rare.notes: Due to acute volume overload from renal artery stenosis

imaging: Catheter-based renal angiography showing 'string of beads' pattern
CT angiography or MR angiography demonstrating multifocal stenosis
Duplex Doppler ultrasound showing elevated renal artery velocities
genetic: No definitive genetic mutation identified; familial cases reported but rare
other: Absence of atherosclerotic plaques on imaging
Possible association with other fibromuscular dysplasia in carotid or vertebral arteries

distinguishingFeatures: Plaque formation on imaging rather than 'string of beads'
Systemic symptoms such as fever and weight loss
Underlying embolic source such as atrial fibrillation

redFlags: Severe or resistant hypertension in young patient
Sudden onset of flank pain with hematuria
Flash pulmonary edema without cardiac cause
references: Olin JW, Gornik HL, Bacharach JM, et al. Fibromuscular Dysplasia: State of the Science and Critical Unanswered Questions: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association. Circulation. 2014;129(9):1048-1078.
Plouin PF, Baguet JP, Thony F, et al. Fibromuscular dysplasia. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2007;2:28.
Persu A, Giavarini A, Touzé E, et al. Diagnosis and management of fibromuscular dysplasia: an expert consensus. Eur J Clin Invest. 2014;44(3):287-306.
